findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning «Den rette og smale vei»
findings.source_quote: “Straight and Narrow,” as ascribed by the early American revival movement
findings.suggested_fix: Change «Den rette og smale vei» to «Den trange og smale vei». In this context “straight” is part of the article’s narrow/strait-gate wordplay, not a claim that the way is morally “right.”

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning «Uavhengig av hvordan vi tolker»
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the paired terms as «trang og smal», keeping the existing HTML tags and order, so the contrast remains about the narrow gate rather than a «rett» (right/straight) way.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning «Her er det en inngang», quoted Luke 12:50
findings.source_quote: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished! –Luke 12:50.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace «og hvor jeg gruer meg til den er fullført!» with a faithful rendering of being constrained or pressed until it is accomplished, for example «og hvor trengt jeg er inntil det er fullført!» Keep the reference as Lukas 12:50.
findings.translation_quote: Men jeg har en dåp jeg må døpes med, og hvor jeg gruer meg til den er fullført! –Lukas 12:50.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning «Gud har gitt mennesker myndighet», quoted Romans 13:1-2
findings.source_quote: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation –Romans 13:1-2.
findings.suggested_fix: Render «damnation» with a Norwegian term that preserves the source’s condemnation meaning, such as «fordømmelse», rather than the less specific «dom». Keep the reference as Romerne 13:1-2.
findings.translation_quote: De som gjør det, skal få sin dom –Romerne 13:1-2.
